# GRAPH_GROWTH

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/graph-growth.md

The live graph and what outlived each navigation climbed at a route's settle on 3 visits to 1.25× — something each visit leaves behind (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `perf`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[GRAPH_GROWTH]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "GRAPH_GROWTH"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

The live graph, counted when each navigation settles, got bigger on every one of the last `data.history.length` visits to `data.route`, and so did the part of it that outlived each of those navigations (`data.survived`, beside `data.history`: what was alive as this or an earlier navigation began and still is) — something each visit creates is never disposed.
A page that is merely bigger on one visit than the last does not report: its content is new at each arrival, so it is not in `data.survived`.
Long-lived module state (a global store, the HMR registry signal of each component in dev) counts the same at every settle once a navigation has met it, so it never climbs.
Navigations that only change a route's params or query continue the visit and are not compared.
This is the leak a heap snapshot finds; the engine finds it by measuring the reactive graph as each navigation opens and at its settle.
`data.grew` says which measure climbed, and that names the leak: `owners` is an undisposed root or a Portal mounted per visit; `computations` with `owners` flat is an effect or memo created with no owner, kept alive only by the sources it reads; `edges` alone is a subscription per visit to something long-lived.
The count is the whole app's, so `data.routes` names every route seen while it climbed; the culprit is on one of them.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

Look for, in order:

* A `createRoot()` in an effect, an event handler, or a module-level helper whose disposer is dropped. Return it from `onSettled` (the component's setup-and-teardown), or call it in `onCleanup`.
* A subscription registered outside the owner that should tear it down — an `addEventListener`, an observer, a store subscription — made in a plain function rather than under the component. Move it under the owner and pair it with `onCleanup`.
* A `Portal`, a panel or a modal mounted on each visit into a long-lived root, never removed when the route leaves.
* A cache (entities kept by key, each under its own root) that only ever adds. Its entries outlive every navigation, so to the walk it is the same growth as a leak, and it is: memory that never comes back. Bound it or evict entries no visit still reads; an evicting cache stays quiet.

Do NOT reach for `dispose()` on the app root or a periodic sweep; the fix is ownership — create the thing under the owner whose lifetime it should share.
`graphSize()` from `solid-js/attribution` gives the count on demand; `OBSERVE.records.subscribe("graph", …)` gives it at every navigation's settle.

The initial route declaration (`initial: true`) emits a `graph` record but is excluded from growth comparisons because it settles before route content mounts.
Later visits to that route count as usual.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `GRAPH_GROWTH` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run, and `expectNoWaste(artifact)` fails on re-runs whose result was unchanged.
Both read the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# HOT_SCOPE_FANOUT

# HOT_SCOPE_RERUNS

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/hot-scope-reruns.md

120+ re-runs of one scope in 1s (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `perf`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[HOT_SCOPE_RERUNS]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "HOT_SCOPE_RERUNS"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A scope re-ran far more often than any UI cadence justifies — a hot signal (often per-frame or per-event) is leaking into it.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

The message names the latest cause; either move that read out of the scope or derive a slower value (e.g. a memo with an equality gate) between them.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `HOT_SCOPE_RERUNS` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run, and `expectNoWaste(artifact)` fails on re-runs whose result was unchanged.
Both read the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# HUGE_FAN_IN

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/huge-fan-in.md

One recompute tracked 2000 sources (always on).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `graph`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[HUGE_FAN_IN]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "HUGE_FAN_IN"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

The always-on backstop: one computation tracked 2000 or more sources in a single pass, so it re-runs when any of them change.
The message names the computation and the count (`data: { count }`); it does NOT list the sources.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

To see which sources, enable the attribution engine and read [`WIDE_SCOPE_DEPS`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/wide-scope-deps), which fires earlier (200 sources) and names up to 12 of them.
The repair is the same: narrow the reads or split the derivation into smaller memos that each track only what they need.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `HUGE_FAN_IN` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run after a write.
It reads the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# HUGE_FAN_OUT

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/huge-fan-out.md

One change reached 2000 live subscribers (always on), or 250 — `fanOut` — on a stamped root write (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `graph`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[HUGE_FAN_OUT]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "HUGE_FAN_OUT"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

One value has very many subscribers, so a single change re-runs all of them (`data.count`).
Always on from 2000; while attribution is enabled the same code fires from `fanOut` (default 250) on a stamped root write, and `data.write` says which — a `write`, a `refresh`, or an `async` landing.
Classic signature: every row of a list comparing against one selected id.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

Invert the question: keep the answer in a store used as a map keyed by id (`selected[row.id]` instead of `row.id === selectedId()`), so each consumer reads its own key and only the keys that flipped update.
When that map is derived from other state, `createProjection` builds it.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `HUGE_FAN_OUT` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run after a write.
It reads the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# IMMUTABLE_UPDATE_IN_STORE

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/immutable-update-in-store.md

Store container replaced by a mostly-identical copy (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `perf`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[IMMUTABLE_UPDATE_IN_STORE]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "IMMUTABLE_UPDATE_IN_STORE"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A store setter replaced a container with a fresh object/array whose leaves are mostly the same values: `draft.user = { ...draft.user, name }`, `draft.items = [...draft.items, x]`, `draft.items = draft.items.filter(…)`.
The store tracks leaves; a fresh container makes every reader of the container's path (anything under `user`) re-run for the one leaf that moved.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

Repair: mutate the draft — `draft.user.name = name`, `draft.items.push(x)`, `draft.items.splice(i, 1)` — so only readers of the touched key or index re-run.
Data arriving from outside (a fetch result for the same records) merges with `reconcile(data, "id")(draft.items)`, which keeps identity for records that did not change.
Once per store path; `data.unchanged/total` says how much of the container was carried over.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `IMMUTABLE_UPDATE_IN_STORE` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run, and `expectNoWaste(artifact)` fails on re-runs whose result was unchanged.
Both read the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.

# LATE_HEADER_WRITE

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write.md

Response header written after the head was sent; dropped (observe + dev; dev throws).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `head`
* **Severity:** `error` (broken behavior)

The console report opens with `[LATE_HEADER_WRITE]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "LATE_HEADER_WRITE"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A response header was written after the head was sent; the write was dropped (dev throws instead).
`data.method`/`data.name` say which.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), `LATE_HEADER_WRITE`, [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Move the write before the first flush — before any `<Loading>` fallback can ship — or before the handler returns; a cookie set from inside a late-streaming component never reaches the browser.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `LATE_HEADER_WRITE` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# LAZY_ASSET_UNMAPPED

A captured artifact from a server render carries both.

## How to fix it

This is bundler-plugin configuration — the plugin injects `$$moduleUrl` and provides the resolver; check the module is under its scope.

## In tests

# LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/loading-on-outside-hold.md

`<Loading on>` changed but its data is also read outside the boundary and holds the frame: the fallback can never be seen.

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `async`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

# LONG_HOLD

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/long-hold.md

Acknowledged hold whose tail (last input → commit) ran 500ms+/1000ms+ (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `responsiveness`
* **Severity:** `info` (advisory, delivered on the diagnostics channel and never printed) or `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[LONG_HOLD]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "LONG_HOLD"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

The hold WAS acknowledged — an `isPending()` spinner, a `latest()` header, an optimistic value — and still ran on: the time from the user's last input to the commit (`data.tailMs`; `holdMs` is the whole wait when input kept arriving) reached `longHolds.infoMs` (default 500ms), `warn` from `longHolds.warnMs` (default 1000ms, where the user loses the thread).
A hold is the stale-while-revalidate tool: right when the old screen stays useful for the wait (tab switch, sort toggle, a fast page turn).
At this length the old screen has stopped being useful and started being a lie; "loading" glued over it reads as broken.

:::note[Responsiveness (from the attribution engine)]
The runtime did the correct thing; the user saw nothing while it did.
These fire only while attribution is enabled.
:::

## How to fix it

Show a fallback instead:

* Put the reader behind a `Loading` boundary keyed on what changed: `<Loading on={page()} fallback={<Skeleton />}>`. With `on`, the write commits at once and the fallback shows where the data lands. Without it a boundary that has already revealed keeps the old content — that IS the hold, so wrapping alone changes nothing.
* A boundary that has not revealed yet (a fresh route segment, a keyed subtree) takes the wait the same way; `on` is the switch for one that has.
* If the data itself is the problem, preload it (`markFlight` the kickoff so it is not misread as a waterfall) or cache it so the tail never gets there.

Do NOT remove the acknowledgement to "fix" this, and do not move the write off the async path.
The measure is the tail, not the lifetime, so a hold that keeps taking input (typing) is judged by each wait, not by the sum.
`feedback().sources[].long`/`longMs` counts these at the table level, acknowledged or not.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `LONG_HOLD` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.
* [Attribution](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/advanced/diagnostics-dev-hooks/attribution): the engine whose records explain a re-run, a hold, or a waterfall.

# LOWERCASE_EVENT_ATTRIBUTE

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/lowercase-event-attribute.md

A function was set on a lowercase `on*` (or `on:`) attribute, which is not an event handler in 2.0; use `onXxx` (dev; client).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `render`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[LOWERCASE_EVENT_ATTRIBUTE]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "LOWERCASE_EVENT_ATTRIBUTE"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A function was set on an attribute whose name starts with `on` but is not an event handler (`data.name`): a lowercase `onclick`, or a leftover 1.x `on:click`.
In 2.0 only `on` + an uppercase letter binds an event; anything else is a plain attribute, so the function was stringified into it and never runs.
Once per attribute name.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Fix: use the camelCase handler (`data.handler` — `onclick={save}` → `onClick={save}`); keep a lowercase name only for a string inline-handler attribute.

# OPTIMISTIC_REVERTED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/optimistic-reverted.md

An optimistic value the screen showed was replaced by a different one — reverted at settle, or superseded by the truth (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `responsiveness`
* **Severity:** `info` (advisory, delivered on the diagnostics channel and never printed)

The console report opens with `[OPTIMISTIC_REVERTED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "OPTIMISTIC_REVERTED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

An optimistic value the screen showed was replaced by a different one: the person saw the guess, then the correction.
`data.how` says which road: `reverted` — the action ended without the guess coming true and the value snapped back to what it covered; `superseded` — the real value landed and differed from the guess (the server counted differently, rejected part of the input).
Both are the runtime doing exactly what optimistic UI promises, which is why this is `info` and never reaches the console; it is a count to read, not a warning to silence.

:::note[Responsiveness (from the attribution engine)]
The runtime did the correct thing; the user saw nothing while it did.
These fire only while attribution is enabled.
:::

## How to fix it

Read it two ways:

* One source, many reverts: the failure is common and the UI is hiding it. Show the failure where the value renders — catch in the action and write an error the UI reads, or put the reader behind an `Errored` boundary — so the snap-back is explained rather than silent.
* One source, many supersessions: the guess is systematically wrong for this input (it ignores what the server adds or normalizes). Guess less: write only the part of the value the client can know, or none, and read `isPending()` for the rest.

Do NOT "fix" a revert by writing the guess to the authoritative signal so it cannot revert — that is not optimistic UI, it is lying to the user about what happened.
The runtime's own optimistic nodes — the `isPending()`/`latest()` companions that acknowledge a hold — are never reported; only values you wrote optimistically are.
Optimistic stores are not covered yet; a store-path revert shows up only as the reader's re-run.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `OPTIMISTIC_REVERTED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
The assertion counts an `info` event like any other, so a scenario that accepts this one lists the code in its `allow` option.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.
* [Attribution](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/advanced/diagnostics-dev-hooks/attribution): the engine whose records explain a re-run, a hold, or a waterfall.

# PRELOAD_DESCRIPTOR_INVALID

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `lifecycle`
* **Severity:** `error` (broken behavior)

The console report opens with `[PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.

# SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized.md

Error replaced with the generic Error on the wire — `data.source` `"server-function"` (`error`) or `"ssr"` (`info`); `data.error` is the original (observe + dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `error` (broken behavior) or `info` (advisory, delivered on the diagnostics channel and never printed)

The console report opens with `[SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

The production wire replaced an error with the generic `Error`; `data.error` is the original, `data.wire` what the client got, and `data.source` says which road:

* `"server-function"` (`error`): a server function threw. Fix the failure it names. If the client is meant to see this error, brand it with `markSafeError` or map it in `wrapInvocation`; do not turn sanitization off.
* `"ssr"` (`info`): a render failure reached the client — an `<Errored>` record, a rejected async source in the stream, a fragment's rejection, a frame's error chunk. Advisory: the failure itself is the [`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained) finding beside it — fix that. If the client is meant to see this error, brand it with `markSafeError`; do not turn sanitization off. A fallback that prints `err().message` shows "Internal Server Error" in production by design.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), `SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`, [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

To *report* these failures from a production build (no `OBSERVE`), register the server error hook — `configureServerErrors({ onError })` from `@solidjs/web` — which hears every handled failure once, and may return the value the client should see instead.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/settled-cleanup-unowned.md

`onSettled` returned a cleanup in an unowned (out-of-band) scope.

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `lifecycle`
* **Severity:** `error` (broken behavior)

The console report opens with `[SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

`onSettled` returned a cleanup while running in an unowned scope, so the cleanup cannot be honored.

## How to fix it

Call the setup helper from an owned scope (the component body), not from an event handler, tracked effect, or another `onSettled`.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# SILENT_HOLD

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/silent-hold.md

Write held 100ms+/200ms+ by pending async with no on-screen acknowledgement (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `responsiveness`
* **Severity:** `info` (advisory, delivered on the diagnostics channel and never printed) or `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SILENT_HOLD]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SILENT_HOLD"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A write landed on async work, so the runtime held it (and everything derived from it) until the data came back — that hold is correct; it is what keeps the screen from tearing.
But for the whole wait nothing on screen acknowledged it: no `isPending()`/`latest()` reader downstream of the write or its blocker, no optimistic value, no `affects()` mark, and no effect ran at all.
From the user's side the click was dead for the duration in the message — which, when the write came from a JSX event handler, starts with what they did (`click on button#next "Next →" wrote "page" (1 → 2)`) and is measured from that event.

:::note[Responsiveness (from the attribution engine)]
The runtime did the correct thing; the user saw nothing while it did.
These fire only while attribution is enabled.
:::

## How to fix it

The fix is ALWAYS to add feedback, never to remove the hold:

* Show the wait: read `isPending(() => blocker())` (the blocker is named in the message) or `isPending(() => derivedFromIt())` in the affected UI and render a busy state from it.
* Reveal the input immediately: `latest(source)` shows the NEW value of the held write (a page number, a filter, a query string) while the data catches up, so the control the user touched reflects the touch.
* Predict the outcome: `createOptimistic`/`createOptimisticStore` written alongside the real write (or inside the action) shows the expected result now and reverts on failure. For actions this is the primary repair — the message says "an action held" when the hold came from one.
* Do NOT: move the write off the async path, wrap it in `untrack`, or split the read so the write commits "faster" — that trades the hold for a torn screen (old data under new controls).

Thresholds sit at the strict end of the band on purpose: the engine measures to the commit, not the paint, so every number is a floor on what the user saw.
From `holds.infoMs` (default 100ms — past "feels instant") the event is `info`-severity, structured channel only; from `holds.warnMs` (default 200ms — the INP "good" ceiling) it reaches the console.
`attribution.history("hold")` lists every hold (acknowledged or not) with what was held, what blocked it, and which affordances answered it; each carries the engine's verdicts as `silent`/`long` fields.
When the silent hold's tail also crossed the long-hold threshold (`data.long: true`) the message carries the [`LONG_HOLD`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/long-hold) repair as well — the fallback is the honest UI at that length.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SILENT_HOLD` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectNoSilentHolds(artifact)` fails on every hold the screen never acknowledged, at any length, not only the ones long enough to warn.
In a budget file the same check is `maxSilentHoldMs: 0`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

## Learn more

* [Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics): every code, with its kind, severity, and trigger.
* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.
* [Attribution](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/advanced/diagnostics-dev-hooks/attribution): the engine whose records explain a re-run, a hold, or a waterfall.

# SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall.md

A `<Loading>` boundary needed 3+/4+ render passes — 2+/3+ sequential async waits (dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `info` (advisory, delivered on the diagnostics channel and never printed) or `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A `<Loading>` boundary rendered in `data.passes` passes — discovery, then one per wait — and each pass past the first is a read that could only start once the previous pass's async answered: `passes - 1` sequential waits, `data.sequentialMs` end to end.
Unlike the client's [`ASYNC_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/async-waterfall) this proof is exact (the pass structure IS the chain), so there is no `markFlight` false positive to rule out.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, `SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL` and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

The same repairs apply, in the same order: derive both reads from the same inputs so they start together (read ALL async sources before using any), or, if the dependency is intrinsic, preload the dependent data or join the requests.
Two waits are `info` — a lead; three or more `warn`.
The boundary is `data.boundary`; a captured artifact has its record in `artifact.records.boundary` (same `id`) and the server-function calls under it in `artifact.records.invocation` (`boundary` field).

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

## Learn more

* [Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics): every code, with its kind, severity, and trigger.
* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.

# SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked.md

Client-only content in a `<Loading>` surfaced only after a server wait; the server's work was discarded (dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A `<Loading>` boundary's content turned out to be client-only (a `ssrSource: "client"` read) but only after `data.passes - 1` real server waits: an async read on an earlier pass masked it.
The server did the work (`data.durationMs`), streamed the fallback, then handed the whole subtree to the client anyway — the work was discarded and the user saw the fallback for the wait, then a client render.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and `SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED` included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Give the client-only read its own `<Loading>` so it hands off with the shell while the async data streams, or read it before the async data so the boundary hands off on its first pass (no finding for that case).

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# SSR_LIVE_HOLE_LATCHED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-live-hole-latched.md

A live hole that shipped its markers was closed by the impurity gate on re-run and stopped updating (dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SSR_LIVE_HOLE_LATCHED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_LIVE_HOLE_LATCHED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A live markup hole (or attribute) in a server component shipped its markers and then stopped updating: re-running it created a reactive scope still waiting on async work (`data.cause: "owners"`) or emitted slot records (`"records"`), so the runtime closed it and the client keeps the markup it last received.
Scopes that finish synchronously (a nested `<For>`, a condition memo such as `{m.usage && …}`, a component) are fine: each re-run gets a throwaway scope.
The usual cause is a memo over a fetch or a stream created inside the markup that re-renders, which would restart on every re-run.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Create the async source in the component body instead.
The finding is located by the component the hole is in.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_LIVE_HOLE_LATCHED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained.md

Server render error routed by a boundary: `data.handling` fallback / client / failed (observe + dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `error` (broken behavior)

The console report opens with `[SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A component threw during a server render and a boundary routed the error; `data.handling` says how.
`fallback` — an `<Errored>` rendered its fallback (the response was a 200 showing the fallback; if this fires on every request the fallback is the page).
`client` — the enclosing `<Loading>` fragment rejected and the client re-rendered the subtree after hydration (the user paid a client render and a flash).
`failed` — nothing contained it and the request failed.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** (`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`, [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

In every case the repair is the error in `data.error`, in the component `ownerPath` names; then consider whether an `<Errored>` closer to the throw would contain it more narrowly.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned.md

Response stream cancelled or sink failed with fragments pending (observe + dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

The client went away (`data.reason: "consumer"`), the sink failed (`"sink"`), or the request's `signal` aborted (`"signal"` — `renderToStream`'s `signal` option, how a frame-stream response learns its reader is gone) while `data.pendingFragments` were still rendering; the render was torn down.
Not an app bug.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), `SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`, [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

At volume it is the cost of renders nobody waited for: make the pending data faster or move it behind navigation.

## In tests

`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.

# SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned.md

A failed fragment's pending descendants were discarded (observe + dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A fragment failed with descendants still pending, and their work (fetches, serialized values — the counts are in `data`) was thrown away; the client rebuilds the subtree.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), `SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`, [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Find the failure (`data.error`), and give the failing read its own `<Loading>` so its siblings ship independently.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

## Learn more

* [Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics): every code, with its kind, severity, and trigger.
* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.

# SSR_UNDECLARED_LIVE_SOURCE

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-undeclared-live-source.md

A document render is still pumping an async iterable in server-component scope 5s in — declare the function `live(...)` or bound the source (dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `ssr`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[SSR_UNDECLARED_LIVE_SOURCE]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "SSR_UNDECLARED_LIVE_SOURCE"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A server component rendered into a document read an async iterable that was still producing `data.afterMs` (5s) later: an undeclared unbounded source pumps into the document and holds it open for as long as it produces.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Declare the server function `live(...)` — the document then takes each source's first value and closes it, and the client connects for the rest after hydration — or bound the source.
Frame-stream renders (a live connection) are never judged.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `SSR_UNDECLARED_LIVE_SOURCE` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# STACKED_HOLDS

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/stacked-holds.md

3+ interactions were waiting in one hold when it committed — repeats piled behind the same source (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `responsiveness`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[STACKED_HOLDS]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "STACKED_HOLDS"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

`data.interactions` interactions were waiting in the same hold when it committed: the person clicked or typed again while the first answer was in the air, and the runtime folded every repeat into one wait on the same source (`data.blockers`).
The pile is the symptom; the hold's own verdict is the cause — check the [`SILENT_HOLD`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/silent-hold)/[`LONG_HOLD`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/long-hold) entry for the same hold first.

:::note[Responsiveness (from the attribution engine)]
The runtime did the correct thing; the user saw nothing while it did.
These fire only while attribution is enabled.
:::

## How to fix it

Then stop the repeats at the control:

* Read `isPending(() => blocker())` where the control renders and disable or dim it while the flight is out, so a second click is not possible.
* For typed input, debounce so a burst of keystrokes is one write.
* Show progress (`latest()` of the input, an optimistic value) so the person does not click again because nothing moved.

Do NOT block input by removing the hold or making the write synchronous; the repeats are a reaction to silence, and the hold is what keeps the screen consistent while the answer arrives.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `STACKED_HOLDS` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

## Learn more

* [Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics): every code, with its kind, severity, and trigger.
* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.
* [Attribution](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/advanced/diagnostics-dev-hooks/attribution): the engine whose records explain a re-run, a hold, or a waterfall.

# STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/strict-read-untracked.md

Untracked reactive read in component/effect body.

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `strict-read`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A reactive value was read outside any tracking scope (e.g. destructured props or a signal called in the component body).
The read got the current value once and will never update.

## How to fix it

Move the read into a tracking scope: JSX, a memo, or an effect's compute function.
If you intentionally want a one-time snapshot, wrap the read in `untrack()` to say so explicitly.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

## How to fix it

Usually a component function inserted where its call was meant, or an object where one of its properties was.

# UNSCOPED_HOLE_ALLOCATED_IDS

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/unscoped-hole-allocated-ids.md

Unscoped hole was handed a function whose content took ids at a position the other side does not share; keys permute (dev).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `render`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[UNSCOPED_HOLE_ALLOCATED_IDS]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "UNSCOPED_HOLE_ALLOCATED_IDS"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A JSX hole was handed a **function** (`data.name`) instead of a value — `const renderHead = () => props.header; <div>{renderHead}</div>` — and calling it built hydratable content.
The compiler scopes every hole that could build JSX so server and client agree on hydration ids, but a bare identifier bound to a function is a value to the compiler and a thunk to the runtime: unscoped, its content takes ids from the enclosing counter where each side happens to evaluate it — the client at the statement, the server in the walk after the scoped holes that follow it reserved theirs — and the keys of its content and of the holes after it permute: detached copies on hydration, dead handlers.
A function hole with nothing scoped after it lands on the same ids both sides and is silent; the finding is the shift.
The server reports it structurally (`data.registered` ≠ `data.before`, the counter's next id when the hole was registered vs. evaluated; `data.after` after it ran), the client when the content it built in place (`data.before` → `data.after`) missed a server-rendered key.
Once per site.
`JSX.Element` excludes functions, so this shape is reached only from JavaScript or through a cast.

:::note[Server rendering]
The server runtime reports on the same channel, with the same `in <App> › <Page>` line.
Two groups.
**Findings** ([`SSR_RENDER_ERROR_CONTAINED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-render-error-contained), [`SSR_SUBTREE_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-subtree-abandoned), [`SSR_STREAM_ABANDONED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-stream-abandoned), [`LATE_HEADER_WRITE`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/late-header-write), [`DYNAMIC_ASYNC_COMPONENT`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/dynamic-async-component), [`SERVER_ERROR_SANITIZED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/server-error-sanitized), [`FRAME_MARKER_CORRUPTED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/frame-marker-corrupted)) are facts about a render that exist in observe builds too — an APM sees them in production; in dev they print.
**Checks** (the rest, [`SSR_BOUNDARY_WATERFALL`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-boundary-waterfall) and [`SSR_CLIENT_CONTENT_MASKED`](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/ssr-client-content-masked) included) are dev-only guidance.
A captured artifact from a server render carries both.
:::

## How to fix it

Fix: call the function at the hole (`{renderHead()}` — a call hole is scoped on both sides) or assign the built value first and insert that.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `UNSCOPED_HOLE_ALLOCATED_IDS` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.

# UNSTABLE_LIST_IDENTITY

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/unstable-list-identity.md

`mapArray`/`For` recreated rows for equivalent items (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Kind:** `perf`
* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[UNSTABLE_LIST_IDENTITY]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "UNSTABLE_LIST_IDENTITY"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A `mapArray`/`<For>` update disposed and recreated most rows while the entering items were field-for-field equivalent to the ones they replaced: a re-fetch (or a spread-copy, see above) handed back fresh objects for the same records, and identity keying treated each as a new row — DOM, state, focus, and scroll position thrown away and rebuilt.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

Repairs: key the list by a stable field (`<For each={rows()} keyed={r => r.id}>`), or merge the data into a store with `reconcile(data, "id")` so the same records keep the same identity.
If a key function is already in use (`data.keyed: true`) it is returning unstable keys (the object itself, or something that changes with the fetch) — return the stable field.
Once per list.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `UNSTABLE_LIST_IDENTITY` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run, and `expectNoWaste(artifact)` fails on re-runs whose result was unchanged.
Both read the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

# UNSTABLE_MEMO_OUTPUT

Source: https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics/unstable-memo-output.md

Memo returned a new-but-equivalent container 4+ runs running (attribution enabled).

## What you saw

* **Severity:** `warn` (code that works but is structurally wrong or expensive)

The console report opens with `[UNSTABLE_MEMO_OUTPUT]` and the message, then an `in` line naming the owners that enclose the subject, root first, and an `at` line with the source location when the code was compiled with one.
In a captured artifact the same finding is an event with `code: "UNSTABLE_MEMO_OUTPUT"`, `ownerPath`, and `loc`.
[Diagnostics](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/reference/solid-js/diagnostics#read-a-report) explains each line.

## Why it fires

A memo keeps producing referentially-new but shallowly-equivalent objects/arrays, so its equality gate never closes and every subscriber re-runs on every upstream change.

:::note[Performance pathologies (from the attribution engine)]
These fire only while attribution is enabled and describe cost, not incorrect behavior.
The numbers in the message are measurements, not guesses.
:::

## How to fix it

Return stable references or pass an `equals` option.

## In tests

`captureArtifact` from `@solidjs/diagnostics` runs a scenario with the diagnostics channel open and returns the events it saw.
`expectNoDiagnostics(artifact)` fails while `UNSTABLE_MEMO_OUTPUT` is among them, with the events as evidence; after the fix, the code is gone from `artifact.diagnostics`.
`expectRerunBudget(artifact, max, { scope })` bounds how often a named scope may re-run, and `expectNoWaste(artifact)` fails on re-runs whose result was unchanged.
Both read the attribution records, which `captureArtifact` collects unless `attribution: false` is passed.
[Check for regressions in tests](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity#check-for-regressions-in-tests) shows the loop and the Vitest matcher form.

* [Debugging reactivity](https://v2-rebuild--solid-docs-v2.netlify.app/guides/debugging-reactivity): how to read a report and what each group of codes points at.
